notes: Fourth sweep (2026-10-22-c, head 3e3581d, uncommitted false): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript reads SKILL.md, then the input, then references/testing.md with Read, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (testing.md) is met in 5 of 5. This case is new in a sweep; the previous sweep has no grade for it, so the capture_log rule and the verdict format follow sweeps/2026-10-22-check-8/grades/log-tests-skill.json and the shared testing rules follow sweeps/2026-10-22-b/grades/test-writing-*.json.

"Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" changed since check-8 by the sentence "Wrap every call that logs, the ones whose return value is under test included, so the suite prints nothing." It is counted separately: 5 of 5 wrap every charge/3 call (check-8: 2 of 4 called it outside any capture in the return-value tests). The rule as a whole is clean in 5 of 5: no :logger.add_handler, StringIO device, backend, Logger.configure or Logger.put_module_level (the primary-level sentence stays unprovoked). Per run: opus-1 captures with with_log/2 in the three return-value tests (lines 44, 64, 85) and capture_log/2 with the asserted call inside in the three log tests; options @log_format [format: "$level $metadata$message
", metadata: [:request_id, :amount_cents], colors: [enabled: false]] (lines 34-38); metadata asserted as separate substrings after a line-anchored level regex (lines 77-79); success absence by capture_log([level: :warning] ++ @log_format, ...) and assert log == "" (lines 53, 57); no call outside a capture. haiku-1 with_log/2 in every test; options [format: "$level $metadata$message
", metadata: :all, colors: [enabled: false]] (line 22); metadata asserted on the single warning line pulled out with assert [warning] = Regex.run(~r/^warning .*card declined$/m, log), then warning =~ "request_id=req_42" and "amount_cents=1999" (lines 61-63); success absence by refute log =~ ~r/^(warning|error) /m (line 41) after an info-line assertion (line 40), a regex that leaves out critical, alert and emergency; no call outside a capture. haiku-2 with_log/2 through a helper charge_with_log/2 (lines 81-85) used by every test; options [format: "[$level] $metadata$message
", metadata: [:request_id, :amount_cents], colors: [enabled: false]] (lines 10-14); metadata asserted as one exact anchored line (line 62, and line 77 for the error); success absence by refute log =~ ~r/^\[(warning|error|critical|alert|emergency)\]/m (line 48) after an exact info-line assertion (line 47); no call outside a capture. sonnet-1 capture_log/1 with no options around the == assertion in the three return-value tests (lines 42, 64, 89) and capture_log(@log_options, ...) with the asserted call inside in the log tests; options [format: "$level $metadata$message
", metadata: [:request_id, :amount_cents], colors: [enabled: false]] (lines 34-38); metadata as separate substrings (lines 80-83); success absence by capture_log([level: :warning] ++ @log_options, ...) and assert log == "" (lines 50, 58); no call outside a capture. sonnet-2 capture_log/1 with no options in the return-value tests (lines 35, 54, 76) and capture_log(@log_options, ...) in the log tests; options [format: "$level $metadata$message
", metadata: :all, colors: [enabled: false]] (line 31); metadata as separate substrings (lines 67-70); success absence by capture_log([level: :warning], ...), with no format options, and assert log == "" (lines 43, 48); no call outside a capture.

As in check-8, each file was also run against five mutants of the input (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error): every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so no log assertion is vacuous; the level: :warning empty captures and the refute regexes both detect a warning on the success path, and sonnet-2's loose assert log =~ "error" (line 89) still fails when the unavailable path logs at warning.

"Assert with patterns" changed since check-8; graded against the current text. The two deciding sentences are counted separately. (a) "In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front, the arrange steps included ... A destructure that cannot fail, such as `{result, log} = with_log(...)`, needs none.": 0 of 5 violate. The only bare matches in test bodies are with_log destructures, which the sentence now exempts by name (opus-1 lines 44, 63, 85; haiku-1 lines 26, 35, 47, 56, 69, 78; haiku-2 lines 39, 45, 54, 60, 68, 74); check-8 needed a judgment for these, the current text decides them. haiku-1 line 2, {:ok, _apps} = Application.ensure_all_started(:logger), is a top-level script line, not a test body, and is not counted. (b) "Put the call under test on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right" (added after 0397dec and unchanged since check-8, where no run broke it): 2 of 5 violate. haiku-1 lines 31, 52, 74: assert {:ok, "ch_1"} == result, with result the destructured return of the call under test; sonnet-2 lines 36-37, 55-56, 77-78: assert {:ok, "ch_123"} == / Charger.charge(...), the rule's backwards shape with the call itself on the right. These put the haiku and sonnet tiers at violated; opus-1 (line 46: assert result == {:ok, "ch_123"}) and sonnet-1 (lines 43-44: assert Charger.charge(...) == / {:ok, "ch_123"}) put the call's value on the left. Judgment: opus-1 binds result through the exempt with_log destructure and compares it whole with ==; I read the "binds the value and an == on it afterwards" sentence as aimed at binding part of a value and comparing that part, which this is not, so opus-1 is clean; reading it literally would make the opus tier violated too. haiku-2 binds result the same way and then asserts a pattern on it (lines 39-41), the two-step shape check-8 graded clean.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state" and "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" are unchanged since check-8 and clean in 5 of 5. opus-1 uses a single describe "charge/3" with condition-bearing test names (line 41: test "returns the charge id when the gateway approves the card"); the other four use describe "charge/3" plus a condition. Every test names a returned value or what was logged; none says only "returns :ok" or "works". All five use async: true with no Logger.configure, Process.register or application env; haiku-1's top-level Application.ensure_all_started(:logger) (line 2) changes no global state the tests share. haiku-1 uses one Payments.Gateway module answering by token; the other four use one module per outcome (opus-1 at top level, the rest nested in the test module).

Outside the case's list: sonnet-1 breaks "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" in its three log tests, where the options keyword list spans several lines inside the call (lines 52-55, 74-77, 99-102), the shape check-8 reported for its haiku-2. Not reported, as in check-8: the nested gateway modules in haiku-2 and sonnet-2 have no @moduledoc false, in an .exs script that builds no docs.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.4, 20 times each with random seeds: every file passed every time (6 tests each) with no compiler warnings and no log line printed to the console, which confirms the wrap-every-call sentence in practice. All five pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json.
